Central to this strategy is the commitment to transition all electricity to renewable energy by 2040, with specific interim targets of 12% renewable energy conversion by 2025, 66% by 2030, and 82% by 2035. The company has already launched 15 vehicles based on the E-GMP platform by 2027, including the EV6 and EV9. Additionally, Kia is establishing a monitoring system for primary suppliers' carbon emissions and will gradually apply low-carbon steel to vehicles starting in 2030.

Kia supports its decarbonization efforts through robust governance structures and incentive systems. The company has established a dedicated Carbon Neutrality Strategy Team under the Sustainability Management Committee of the Board of Directors, with the Head of Corporate Strategy assigned oversight responsibilities. Climate-related KPIs are integrated into executive compensation, with the CEO and major division heads evaluated annually on climate change mitigation performance. The RE100 implementation follows a structured four-phase review process, from electricity use forecasting to establishing PPA/REC strategies, ensuring systematic progress toward the company's renewable energy targets.

The company has established robust governance structures including the Risk Management and Sustainability Committee (RMSC), Chief Sustainability Officer (CSO), and the Sustainability Steering Committee (SSC) established in 2023 to drive sustainability-focused initiatives. Their strategy follows a three-phase transition approach (short, medium, and long term) to manage the transition to a low-carbon economy, with specific attention to both physical climate risks and transition risks. The company aligns its net-zero pathway with the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi), focusing on reducing emissions before addressing any remaining carbon through removal or offsetting measures.

The company is implementing several concrete decarbonization initiatives in 2024. They have invested RM108 million in upgrading their state-of-the-art bottling line to optimize energy usage and reduce waste management, achieving zero waste to landfill. Additionally, they've installed a RM11.6 million new Beer Membrane Filtration System to reduce energy usage in processing operations, and invested RM80.4 million in a new energy-efficient canning line. They've also implemented a new Cleaning in Place (CIP) plant that centralizes tank cleaning to enhance energy efficiency and optimized groundwater purification to utilize less energy. The company is actively exploring renewable energy boilers and purchasing low-carbon electricity supply from TNB to reduce reliance on fossil fuels. For physical climate risks, they're allocating resources for infrastructure upgrades including flood-resistant buildings and drainage systems to address riverine and rainfall-driven flooding risks.

To support their decarbonization efforts, the company has begun collecting data for Scope 3 carbon emissions and aims to reduce value chain emissions per hectolitre by 30% by 2030 from a 2015 baseline. In 2024, they've achieved Cradle to Cradle Certified™ at the Silver level for better recycling, with over 95% of bottles collected from trade for recycling and recycled content reaching 60% and 50% in bottles and cans respectively. The company is also converting natural gas boilers to renewable energy boilers within the next two years and investing RM8 million in groundwater purification capacity to ensure water security. Their approach integrates climate considerations into business strategy, with specific mitigation efforts for both physical and transition risks across short, medium, and long-term horizons.

The company utilizes oil palm fiber to generate renewable energy in boilers for milling processes while repurposing empty fruit bunches, decanter solids, and boiler ash for soil management to improve nutrient content in estates. To support this transition, they established a dedicated Sustainability Committee to oversee climate-related risk management and strategy development, while investing in innovative technologies that reduce emissions and improve resource efficiency. The company also conducts regular climate risk assessments to identify and evaluate climate-related risks and opportunities, aligning their reporting with IFRS S2 framework requirements to enhance emissions transparency.

The bank also became the first in Malaysia to enable contactless credit or debit card payments for EV charging, removing barriers to electric vehicle adoption.

To support the decarbonization strategy, CIMB has established strategic partnerships with over 10 prominent business chambers and associations, including the Federation of Malaysian Manufacturers and Malaysia Aquaculture Development Association. These collaborations enhance access to financing and resources for SMEs to adopt Industry 4.0 practices and integrate digital, high-tech, and low-carbon strategies. strategy_summary:
Fubon Financial's decarbonization strategy for 2024 centers on a comprehensive approach to transform its investment and loan portfolios while supporting clients' transition to low-carbon operations. The company has established clear phase-out timelines for high-carbon investments, with commitments to eliminate investments in coal-related sources by 2030 (for companies deriving more than 5% of revenue from coal) and unconventional oil and gas by 2040. This approach is guided by the 'Fubon Financial Holding Co., Ltd. and Subsidiaries Sustainable Finance Policy,' which serves as their highest guiding principle for promoting sustainable finance. The strategy includes concrete portfolio management measures such as capping investments in 'high' ESG risk assets and high carbon industries at 22% within active funds, targets that were achieved in 2024. Fubon has also established credit standards that restrict funding for five high-carbon industries—power generation, coal mining, cement, petrochemicals, and steel—except when the funds support low-carbon transition, green energy development, or carbon reduction efforts. To accelerate this transition, Fubon has set a goal of NT$2.9 trillion in green finance by 2030, having already exceeded NT$2.5 trillion in 2024 through low-carbon investments, green energy technology investments, green bonds, and green financing.

Fubon's strategy extends beyond portfolio management to active client engagement and capacity building. In 2024, the company organized an SBT (Science-Based Targets) engagement workshop with over 30 corporate customers, focusing on setting Science-Based Targets for carbon reduction. They also hosted 'SME Net-zero Emissions Workshops' for small and medium-sized enterprises, attended by 107 representatives from 72 companies. The company has implemented a three-tiered ESG assessment mechanism for investments, including pre-investment checks (establishing blacklists/exclusion lists), post-investment monitoring, and verification of foreign discretionary investment institutions' ESG practices. Additionally, Fubon has joined the Partnership for Biodiversity Accounting Financials (PBAF) to assess the impact of investments on biodiversity, demonstrating an integrated approach to environmental sustainability.

To support implementation, Fubon has established governance structures including an ESG assessment mechanism with three lines of defense, and has integrated decarbonization into its core business operations across all subsidiaries. The company tracks renewable energy consumption, using 16.56 million kWh in 2024 (accounting for 16.4% of total electricity consumption), and has set specific targets for renewable energy adoption. Fubon's strategy is validated through international recognition, including being named to the DJSI World Index for the eighth consecutive year and maintaining an 'AA' MSCI ESG Index rating. The company also actively supports clients through green financing options, with Fubon Insurance providing corporate clients with loss prevention services for green energy risks and supporting green energy transitions through premium discounts.

strategy_summary:
Ajiya Berhad’s 2024 decarbonization strategy is grounded in operational integration of renewable energy, energy efficiency, and green construction practices, aligned with Malaysia’s 12th Malaysia Plan, the Paris Agreement, and national frameworks like the National Energy Policy 2022–2040. The company prioritizes concrete actions, including deploying solar photovoltaic systems across most Malaysian factories and implementing energy-efficient technologies to reduce emissions. A cornerstone initiative is Ajiya Green Integrated Building Solutions (AGiBS), developed through its Metal and Glass Divisions, which offers integrated construction methods to enhance productivity while promoting green building practices in line with CIDB’s initiatives. The strategy also emphasizes adherence to global standards, with the company adopting Taskforce on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) recommendations and transitioning to IFRS S2 to strengthen climate risk management. In December 2024, Ajiya conducted a Climate Risk Assessment to evaluate exposure to climate-related risks, ensuring strategic decisions are informed by comprehensive risk analysis.

Supporting these efforts is a structured governance framework: the Board of Directors sets long-term sustainability direction, while the Management Team and Sustainability Management Committee (SMC) implement strategies, assess climate-related risks, set targets, and monitor progress. The SMC ensures alignment with regulatory expectations and industry best practices, with on-ground teams enforcing sustainability controls across departments. Beyond internal operations, Ajiya collaborates externally as a founding member of the Malaysia Green Building Council and has been recognized by the Ministry of Environment and Water for its role in managing ozone-depleting substances under the Montreal Protocol. These multi-layered initiatives reflect a commitment to embedding decarbonization into core operations, governance, and sector-wide partnerships to drive long-term resilience and low-carbon growth.

Bhd., Sarawak Energy) and fuel sources (Smartpay Petronas) alongside recognized conversion factors for energy measurement. strategy_summary:
Frontken Group's decarbonization strategy for 2024 is structured around three strategic pillars: climate resilience, resources resilience, and production resilience. The company has adopted a comprehensive approach that integrates climate responsibility across all business units while aligning with international frameworks including the Paris Agreement and Science-Based Targets Initiative (SBTi). Frontken has established specific commitments to reduce energy consumption in operations through building energy efficiency improvements, implement renewable energy technologies such as solar photovoltaic systems across facilities, and minimize water impacts through water-efficient technologies. The company has declared a net-zero emissions target by 2050 and is using SBTi to set science-based targets for limiting global warming to well below 2°C, with efforts to stay below 1.5°C.

To operationalize this strategy, Frontken has implemented concrete initiatives including the establishment of a Sustainability Steering Committee, integration of climate considerations into enterprise risk management frameworks, and systematic assessment of climate-related financial impacts through the TCFD framework. The company is actively engaging with stakeholders across the supply chain to minimize carbon impacts and has committed to reporting greenhouse gas emissions in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol. Frontken is also investing in R&D for sustainable innovation and working with industry associations to implement green energy technologies.

The governance structure supporting this strategy includes Board-level oversight for climate strategy, with the Board of Directors responsible for strategic oversight, risk management, and performance monitoring of climate-related objectives. The Audit Committee ensures accurate assessment and disclosure of climate-related risks in financial statements, while the company has established specific metrics for climate-related performance monitoring. Frontken's approach demonstrates a commitment to both reducing operational emissions and addressing Scope 3 emissions through supply chain engagement, with all initiatives designed to support the company's overarching goal of reducing its environmental footprint while contributing to global climate change mitigation efforts.

strategy_summary:
IJM Corporation's decarbonization strategy for 2024 centers on its Climate Strategy R₂O, introduced in April 2023, which applies a two-pronged approach addressing both climate mitigation and adaptation. The company has established specific net-zero targets across all emission scopes: Scope 1 by 2050, Scope 2 by 2035 via 100% renewable electricity, and operational Scope 3 emissions by 2050, while engaging the supply chain for embedded Scope 3 emissions reduction by 2027. These targets align with Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) guidelines but include some deviations to accommodate business-specific constraints.

The company has implemented several concrete initiatives to achieve these targets, including increasing renewable energy generation capacity to 8,050 kWp through solar photovoltaic panels at multiple facilities, and successfully replacing 13% of cement content with non-cementitious material in its Industry Division. IJM has established a comprehensive reduction strategy across four key focus areas: Energy Optimisation (exploring alternative fuels and electrification), Supply Chain Advocacy (reducing waste and engaging suppliers), Industry Engagement (collaborating with industry associations), and Product Stewardship (incorporating sustainable design principles). The company has also formalized its Risk Management and Sustainability Committee (RMSC) to provide strategic oversight and ensure integration of climate considerations into enterprise risk management.

Supporting these initiatives, IJM has built internal capacity for carbon accounting across all business divisions, established a Group carbon inventory based on FY2022 emissions, and enhanced Scope 3 disclosures. The company is developing a sustainability dashboard to enable comprehensive performance management and has expanded its organizational boundaries to include operations in India. Additionally, IJM is implementing the Kuantan Green Port Initiative, which has reduced diesel usage by 34,106 liters through electric shore power supply, and has developed low-carbon emission products with green certifications such as SIRIM ECO Labelling and Singapore Green Label.

bp's 2024 decarbonization strategy centers on two core net zero aims: achieving net zero for operations (Scope 1 and 2 emissions) and for the energy products it sells, both by 2050 or sooner. The company has established interim targets including a 20% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions by the end of 2025 against the 2019 baseline, with a 2030 target of approximately 45% reduction. bp has refined its approach by retiring previous aims to focus on these two priority areas, which it considers most relevant to long-term success. The strategy emphasizes maintaining 'near-zero' methane intensity across operated producing assets and reducing the average lifecycle carbon intensity of energy products sold through supportive government policies and energy demand decarbonization.

To implement this strategy, bp has launched several concrete initiatives. The company is scaling up bio-based fuels production, including signing a 10-year agreement with MIGASA in Spain for 40,000 tonnes annually of non-food industrial waste to support bio-based fuel production at its Castellón Refinery. It has finalized a Nature-based Solutions (NbS) action plan to embed nature into engineering designs for new and existing operations, while supporting projects like the Kafue-Zambezi Community Forest Project and the World Bank's Forest Carbon Partnership Facility. bp is also implementing circular economy principles across its business, with initiatives including making food packaging recyclable by 2025 and diverting over one million kilograms of surplus food from waste. The company has established a new methane measurement approach, achieving a methane intensity of 0.07 in 2024.

bp supports its decarbonization efforts through robust governance structures and strategic partnerships. The company evaluates all new material capex investments greater than $250 million against Paris goals through its Risk Committee. It has updated its risk classification system to reflect changing sustainability risks and maintains a dedicated sustainability governance structure overseeing delivery across businesses. bp collaborates with academic partners through initiatives like the Carbon Mitigation Initiative and Sustainable Markets Initiative, and works with communities on just transition projects such as the Aberdeen Hydrogen Hub. The company also continues to develop its operating management system to embed circularity principles and sustainability considerations across all operations.

The company has also improved Scope 3 data quality through this travel management solution, which cuts across all jurisdictions.

Supporting these initiatives is a robust governance framework where the Business Ethics and Sustainability Committee (BESC) oversees the decarbonization strategy and regularly reports to the Group Management Team and Supervisory Board. Through their subsidiary Plenitude Energy Services (PES), they delivered comprehensive energy efficiency solutions including photovoltaic system management, smart home products, and heating/cooling services across Italy, France, Greece, and Spain. strategy_summary:
S P Setia Berhad's decarbonization strategy for 2024 centers on a structured, science-based approach to achieve net zero emissions by 2050, with clear interim targets for Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions. The company has established 2024 as the baseline year for emissions tracking and committed to a 45% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 carbon emissions by 2030 and 70% by 2040. For Scope 3 emissions, they target a 20% reduction in embodied carbon emissions (measured by intensity) by 2030 for landed properties. The strategy is grounded in the GHG Protocol framework with specific baselines of 487 kgCO₂e/m² for landed properties and 1,044 kgCO₂e/m² for high-rise properties, and incorporates Malaysia-specific climate data for scenario analysis to identify physical and transition risks.

The company is implementing several concrete initiatives to drive emissions reduction. They established the eDew system in 2024 to digitalize emissions data collection and monitoring across business units, enhancing accuracy and transparency. The Setia eGreenLiving initiative integrates EV-ready infrastructure, solar panel installations, and energy-efficient building designs across developments. Their sustainable landscaping approach prioritizes native plants, green corridors, and water-efficient practices like rainwater harvesting, while composting vegetation waste for fertilizer use. The company also implemented the Setia Biodiversity Policy (to be finalized by mid-2025) and introduced Tree Planting Guidelines for Carbon Sequestration aligned with IUCN Red List standards.

To support this strategy, S P Setia has established a comprehensive governance framework with the Sustainability Committee overseeing strategy and targets, and the Sustainability Working Group implementing ESG initiatives across business units. The company is aligning with TCFD recommendations and progressively adopting IFRS S2 standards for climate-related financial disclosures. Their climate risk assessment process, embedded within the Enterprise Risk Management Framework, evaluates both physical and transition risks through scenario analysis, with specific attention to heat impacts in coming decades. The Setia Green Roadmap provides the structured pathway for achieving emissions reduction targets while maintaining business resilience.

The company utilizes advanced monitoring systems to provide daily information supporting operational decisions and measuring progress toward annual flaring goals. Through collaboration with midstream partners, they address infrastructure limitations that can lead to flaring.
